messages.author: acc155ea1886618f
messages.subject: Negative factor scores with lavPredict
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm working with a set of survey data which has up to 20% missing data and I did multiple imputation in MICE before running a CFA with semTools and getting the factor score with lavPredict.
The survey data contains questions on motivation and learning attitudes and they are on a scale from 1-5. I specified in MICE that the imputation value should fall within the plausible range of value 1-5.
The factor scores that I obtained with lavPredict contain negative values and other values that were not within the range of 1-5.
What might be a possible reason for this and how can I solve it?

I have added my codes to provide a better context.

mice.imp <- NULL
for(i in 1:20) mice.imp[[i]] <- complete(imp, action=i, inc=FALSE) 

library(lavaan)
HS.model <- ' MAPG  =~ mapg1 + mapg2 + mapg3'


library(semTools)
out2 <- runMI(HS.model, 
              data=mice.imp,
              fun="cfa",
              meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(out2)
lavPredict(out2, fsm = TRUE)

Thanks in advance for your help!

Yvonne

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Negative factor scores with lavPredict
parts:
Yvonne

Having negative factor scores is not unexpected, the factor scores are in the metric of the latent variable, not the items. If you use std.lv=T, the latent variable will be in a standardize metric with mean =0 and  sd=1, which will have people with negative numbers. If you use fix loading (the default) the latent variable will be in function of the 1 variable loading that is fix to 1, subjects with low scores in function of that variable will have negative numbers, and depending of which variable is chosen this will change

If you want to have the have the latent variable with the same metric as your items you need to use effects coding as your method of identification.

bye
